ambiguities.text: The specification does not define what error response (if any) an eth/67 client should send when receiving a GetNodeData request
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume eth/67 clients should either ignore the message or disconnect the peer for protocol violation. Implementation may vary between clients.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'older clients can continue using eth/66' does not specify for how long or what compatibility guarantees exist
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume eth/66 support will be maintained until the majority of the network has upgraded, after which eth/66 peers may become increasingly rare.

implicit_assumptions.description: All clients that need state sync functionality have implemented the snap protocol before upgrading to eth/67
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Clients upgrading to eth/67 without snap support would be unable to perform state synchronization, potentially causing sync failures

implicit_assumptions.description: Sufficient eth/66 or snap-capable peers exist in the network during the transition period
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: New or syncing nodes might be unable to obtain state data if they cannot find compatible peers

implicit_assumptions.description: The removal of GetNodeData does not create new attack vectors compared to snap protocol
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If snap protocol has different security properties than GetNodeData, this could change the threat model for state sync
